[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant discusses the founding of Carnegie Steel by Andrew Carnegie in 1892 and its significance for Pennsylvania's industrial landscape, citing Livesay (2007, p. 96) and Nasaw (2006, p. 122).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explains that Carnegie Steel's success was due to innovative management practices and investment in new technology, leading to job opportunities for Pennsylvanians (Livesay, 2007, p. 101).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant describes Frederick Taylor's theory of workplace efficiency, known as Scientific Management or Taylorism, and its impact on industrial productivity (Kanigel, 1997, p. 48).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant notes that Taylor's methods were adopted by many Pennsylvania companies, increasing productivity but also leading to labor unrest (Kanigel, 1997, p. 60, 65).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant details the Three Mile Island catastrophe on March 28, 1979, and its implications for Pennsylvania's energy sector, citing Walker (2004, p. 108).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentions that the incident raised questions about safety protocols and long-term health effects for nearby residents (Walker, 2004, p. 118).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant states that the Three Mile Island incident prompted a reevaluation of Pennsylvania's energy policies and increased interest in alternative energy sources (Walker, 2004, p. 142, 147).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Assistant concludes the paper by emphasizing the importance of balancing industrial ambition with responsibility and the lessons learned from Pennsylvania's history.
